subject: POC enablement plan & MAP milestones — env, keys, peering
messages:
From: Elaine Carter <elaine@medsync.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Perez <tom.perez@medsync.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + MAP kickoff: POC environment requirements

Hi Rachel / Aditya,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency numbers. Tom and I discussed next steps and wanted to kick off a short MAP so we can lock the POC environment and close timeline. High level asks from our infra/security side: API key provisioning, org-level account setup, a small IP allowlist template, and VPC peering guide for our AWS account. We have a 4-week evaluation window and need the environment ready by next Monday if possible.

Attaching a basic spreadsheet with our proposed test cases. Can you confirm who on your side will own the peering coordination and whether we should open an ingress ticket with our cloud team?

Thanks,
Elaine Carter
Director of Platform Ops | MedSync Health
elaine@medsync.com

Attachments: medsync-poc-testcases.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Carter <elaine@medsync.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + MAP kickoff: POC environment requirements

Hi Elaine — great to hear. We're happy to move quickly. Quick outline of what we'll deliver and owners: 

- Org & API keys: we will create a MedSync org in our console and provision two API keys (one for integration, one for tests). Owner: Rachel Kim (platform onboarding).
- IP allowlist: please send a list of public egress IPs; we will add to the temporary allowlist. Owner: Aditya Rao (network infra).
- VPC peering: we support AWS VPC peering and cross-account routing. We'll need your VPC ID, CIDR, and an admin contact to coordinate route tables. Owner: Rishi Malhotra (network partner).
- Timeline: aim to have environment ready by 2026-05-10 for your first test run. If there are any procurement constraints we can adjust the MAP.

I've attached a short MAP doc that maps milestones to owners and dates. Next step: can you confirm the VPC details and provide the IP allowlist CSV?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-map-v1.pdf (MAP summary)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: MedSync POC — network prep checklist

Folks — forwarding Elaine's ask. I'll own the allowlist change but need Rishi to confirm peering feasibility for the proposed CIDR (10.12.0.0/16) and whether we need a Transit Gateway. Initial checklist I propose: 

1) Provision temporary MedSync org + API keys (Rachel)
2) Create a sandbox VPC and whitelist MedSync egress IPs (Aditya)
3) Validate peering config and cross-account IAM role for route updates (Rishi)
4) Prepare a runbook for test cases and token rotation schedule (Soojin)

If we can get the VPC ID and nominal CIDR by EOD tomorrow we can hit the 5/10 target. I'll draft the Change ticket for the allowlist.

- Aditya

On Mon, May 3, 2026 at 10:05 AM Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Elaine — great to hear. We're happy to move quickly. Quick outline...
From: Tom Perez <tom.perez@medsync.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Carter <elaine@medsync.com>
Date: 2026-05-04T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + MAP kickoff: POC environment requirements

Thanks — here's the info you requested.

- VPC ID: vpc-0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b
- CIDR: 10.12.0.0/16
- Admin contact: cloud-admin@medsync.com (Samir Patel)
- IP allowlist (public egress): see attached CSV with 3 /24 blocks and a couple of NAT gateways.

We prefer peering directly (no TGW) for this POC; let us know if that causes routing issues on your side. Also flagged the HubSpot deal for the procurement team — they may request a short SOW.

Cheers,
Tom Perez
Infrastructure Engineer | MedSync Health

Attachments: poc-ip-allowlist-template.csv (CSV stub)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Perez <tom.perez@medsync.com>, Elaine Carter <elaine@medsync.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-05T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + MAP kickoff: POC environment requirements

Tom / Elaine — thanks for the details. Quick update from infra: direct VPC peering for the CIDR you provided is acceptable for the sandbox POC, but we need to add the following items to the MAP before we flip routes: 

- Exchange a cross-account IAM role ARN (we'll provide a template role that grants route table modification for the specific peering connection).
- Confirm no overlapping subnets on your side beyond the supplied CIDR; overlapping will block peering.
- Set a 72-hour maintenance window for initial route propagation (we'll schedule it for 5/09 02:00-05:00 UTC if that works).
- We'll provision two API keys in the MedSync org with expiry set to 60 days and a rotation note in the runbook.

Action items for MedSync: send the IAM role ARN or allow our security team to create the role, and confirm the maintenance window. I'll create the peering request once the role is in place.

I'll also attach a short peering checklist and the redwood MAP doc with the updated target dates.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Network Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Attachments: vpc-peering-reqs.docx (peering checklist), redwood-map-v1.pdf (updated)
